title: The props a section's view receives
description:
Tier 4 of the customisation ladder (README, 'The customisation ladder'). A client site that swaps a section's view keeps the section's logic, and the logic hands the view exactly these props, so a swapped view is written against a stable public type. Every view receives two things: `data`, described in contract/view-props/<section id>.json, and `plan`, the page plan's view of the section, described once as the `plan` type in contract/view-props/_shared.json. Salt for Next.js generates a TypeScript interface per file ({ data: <Section>Data; plan: Plan }, names in PascalCase) and Salt for WordPress a PHP array shape (array{data: array{...}, plan: array{...}}) for its view templates' docblocks and static analysis. Retyping or removing a prop is MAJOR, a new nullable prop MINOR (RELEASE-POLICY.md section 2).

KINDS map to both languages and are the only ones allowed. text: string. integer: int. number: int|float (TypeScript number). boolean: bool. enum: one of `values`, which are strings or integers. icon: a content icon name from contract/sections.json `icons`, as a string. rich-text: the field's body, as the platform's own renderer takes it (Salt for Next.js: Lexical's JSON; Salt for WordPress: sanitised HTML); a view hands it to the platform's rich-text renderer and never parses it. object: a value of the named type in `of`. list: an ordered array of `of`, which is a type or a scalar kind. A `nullable` prop is null when it has no value (SC-009 says when text is empty), never an empty string; a list is never null unless `nullable` says so, and is empty instead.

WHERE A PROP COMES FROM (`from`). field: the editor's value, cleaned (trimmed, emptied text as null, choices narrowed to their options), named by `field` and taking that field's name. logic: computed by the section's logic, from `field` where one is named. collection: items read from a collection, by the query `field` names. site: a site setting outside the section (contact details, labels). plan: the page plan (heading level, the settled anchor, priority media). The package gate (scripts/check_salt_extensions.mjs) checks: every section in contract/sections.json has a file and no file names another; every `field` names a real field in the section's fields file, through groups and list rows by dots (`buttons.link`), or a shared setting as `settings.<name>`; a `from: field` prop takes the field's name, and is nullable whenever its field can clean or resolve to nothing (a text, textarea, rich-text, image, link, relationship or number field, required or not, since SC-009 empties whitespace-only text and an upload can be deleted; or a select with no default that is not required); a non-null value backed by such a field comes `from: logic`, with a description saying how the logic guarantees it (it drops the row); an enum prop drawn from a select offers exactly its options; every `of` names a type in the file or in _shared.json, or a scalar kind.

of.description: For object, the type's id; for list, a type's id or a scalar kind.

formerly.description: The type or variable this platform's view received before the contract.

owes.description: What this platform must add or change to conform.

section.description: The section id, which is also the file name; `shared` for _shared.json, which holds only types.

types.description: Named object types, by id. A section file's types are its own; _shared.json's are every file's.
